summary: Lamar County, AL site the state acquired in 1949 for a lookout that was never built; the state sold the land in 1998 and a private landowner now administers it.

facts.status_note: Never built: the state planned a lookout on this site in 1949, but none was constructed

access.note: Register lists a private landowner as administrator; no visitor access described

events.note: State of Alabama acquired the site to build a lookout; the lookout was never constructed
Registered November 27, 2016; nominated by Andrew Zerbe

evidence.supports: state acquired the site in 1949 to build a lookout
evidence.quote: The State of Alabama acquired this site in 1949 to build a lookout
The state sold the land in 1998.

evidence.supports: photo captioned as the site of a planned lookout
photo supplied by Andrew Zerbe (courtesy credit)

corrections.why: The register says the lookout was never constructed, so no tower stood here to be gone. 'never_built' is not an existing status value and would need adding.

notes_for_editor: Single source: the FFLOS entry. The register's name 'Kingsville' matched no place I could confirm. Wikipedia's Kingville, Lamar County (33.6675, -88.0406) is roughly 5 km from the register point; no source ties the site to that community, so it is not used. The owner is not named. The proposed status 'never_built' needs a new enum value. One WebSearch found nothing about the site; Lamar County records or the Alabama Forestry Commission would be the next check.
